# Moonsault Sun/Moon extended independent oracle, 2026-11-04

Architecture: Tom Dyer. ooRexx ephemeris implementation: ChatGPT (GPT-6).

Source under test: packages/oorexx_moonsault_v0.1/src/MoonsaultEphemeris.cls.
Runtime: ooRexx 5.3.0 r13196 extracted from user-provided .deb.
Independent reference: Swiss Ephemeris 2.10.03 with topocentric observer at 0m,
1010 hPa and 10 C, swe.calc_ut(SUN|MOON, FLG_EQUATORIAL|FLG_TOPOCTR),
swe.azalt(EQU2HOR). Swiss reference is validation only, not in ooRexx runtime.

Test set: 15th of each month January-December 2026 at 00,06,12,18 UTC,
cycling among Sydney (-33.8688,151.2093), London (51.5074,-0.1278),
Melbourne (-37.8136,144.9631).
48 times * 2 bodies = 96 body-time cases = 192 altitude/azimuth comparisons.

MAX ABSOLUTE DIFFERENCE:
Sun altitude 0.009237 deg; Sun azimuth 0.013243 deg.
Moon altitude 0.057653 deg; Moon azimuth 0.073233 deg.

Acceptance thresholds: 0.10 deg Sun component, 0.30 deg Moon component.
Exceedances 0. 
Earlier six fixed reference cases, explicit test_ephemeris.rex: 24/24
angle comparisons within thresholds; visibility and J2000 checks PASS.

Boundaries: spherical/sea-level lunar parallax, low-precision orbital terms,
standard-atmosphere refraction (poor near horizon), UTC as approximate UT1,
no actual measured photographic bearings, no field navigation acceptance.
This is a finite test set, not a global accuracy proof and not a claim
of 25m geodetic position accuracy.

SLAM450 interface contract: camera detection is independent, ephemeris prediction
source tag MOONSAULT_PREDICTED is not an observation, and only the SLAM450
camera+flight-book component can publish SUN_HEADING or MOON_HEADING.
